newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs resume counting votes in Bosnia election.
newsitem.headline: Serbs resume counting votes in Bosnia election.

text.p: International election supervisors in Bosnia said on Sunday Serb officials had dropped a complaint about refugee ballots and that counting had resumed in Serb territory.
Sir Kenneth Scott, deputy head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Bosnia, said the complaint was the "result of a misunderstanding".

"The provisional election commission determined that this request was due to a misundertstanding of the election procedure", Scott told reporters after meeting Bosnian Serb election commission officials in Pale outside Sarajevo.
OSCE spokeswoman Nicole Szulc said in Sarajevo that counting got under way again at 2.45 p.m. (1245 GMT) following an OSCE trouble-shooting trip to the Serb stronghold of Pale.

Svetislav Stanojevic, president of the Bosnian Serb electoral commission, had alleged that local commissions had received bags of ballots from refugee voters without proper documents accompanying them.

"It was a genuine misunderstanding. We have sorted it out, and now the provisional election commission will instruct the local election commissions...that counting should begin at once in all the counting centres where all the ballots have arrived," Scott said, standing next to Stanojevic.
Scott did not specify if the announcement of results would be delayed by the Serb complaint. "It will obviously cause some delay but I hope not too much."
He said there was no reason for the Serbs to stop counting ballots and that all complaints would be examined before the final results are announced.

Stanojevic also described the issue as a misunderstanding, but it remained unclear if the Serbs were dropping their objections. He said he had ordered counting centres to accept bags of ballots from refugees and he added "there was no intention to delay the election process".

Bosnia's main Moslem party said on Saturday it would not accept voting results on Serb territory due to alleged vote fraud. First preliminary results from the elections are expected to be announced on Monday.
